evals.prompt: Review this design doc for our new booking service and tell me if it is ready to build.
evals.expected_output: Scores the nine axes with cited evidence, marks unsupported claims as unverified or otherwise not established, traces the critical path end to end, and returns a verdict plus a prioritized roadmap.

assertions.description: Scores against a fixed axis set
Refuses to score intent as evidence without requiring an exact status word
Converts gaps into prioritized action

evals.prompt: Checkout p95 is 1.2 seconds. Traces from the same period show the pricing call at 800 ms p95 and the database at 100 ms p95. The team proposes a Go/microservices rewrite. What should be investigated or changed first?
evals.expected_output: Use the measured path to investigate pricing-call time and confirm it is part of the user-visible 1.2-second checkout path; inspect call timing and failure behavior before choosing a remedy. Recommend a change only when it removes measured delay; these measurements alone do not justify a rewrite.

assertions.description: Uses the observed largest span as investigation evidence
Keeps the service span tied to the end-to-end result
Does not infer a rewrite from latency evidence alone

evals.prompt: A 40-person internal admin tool serves 100 requests/s and has no stated cross-region recovery objective. Its proposed data migration can irreversibly lose existing records and has no tested rollback. Which finding should be addressed first?
evals.expected_output: Prioritize the migration's untested rollback because it exposes existing records to irreversible loss; establish a recoverable migration/restore path before release. Do not fail the tool solely for lacking multi-region when no cross-region objective is stated.

assertions.description: Prioritizes the concrete irreversible data-loss risk
Does not impose an unstated regional recovery requirement

evals.prompt: Review an accurate text-only design that enumerates actors, trust boundaries, data, interfaces and failure paths. No visual artifact was requested and no view is missing. Return JSON with redraw_required and review_complete.
evals.expected_output: Complete the semantic review without a redraw prerequisite (for example, {"redraw_required":false,"review_complete":true}). If a view is genuinely missing, identify that specific gap rather than fabricating a diagram requirement.

assertions.description: Checks text-only completeness does not create an unnecessary diagram prerequisite.
Checks the unnecessary redraw does not block the requested semantic review.

evals.prompt: A booking proposal states its no-double-booking mechanism and 15 RPS target, but omits owner, capacity, cost, rollout and recovery detail. It is not deployed. Evaluate what conclusion the available evidence supports.
evals.expected_output: Treats the mechanism as proposed design evidence, identifies missing material design inputs, and avoids claiming deployment or operational readiness from documentation.

assertions.description: Keeps source evidence category explicit
Surfaces evidence gap without pinning a status label

evals.prompt: A team says its booking service has measured recovery, but provides neither a dated drill result nor observed journey SLO data. What does this support?
evals.expected_output: Does not support the claimed recovery or operations conclusion without corresponding measured evidence; identifies the relevant gap and distinguishes it from a proposed recovery plan.

assertions.description: Names relevant evidence needed for operations claim
Rejects unsubstantiated operations claim

evals.prompt: A reservation must not confirm two customers for the same seat; sending a receipt can fail independently. Choose mechanisms and explain the boundary.
evals.expected_output: Requires an authoritative mechanism that preserves unique reservation, permits a separately justified notification path, and ensures notification failure cannot undo a confirmed booking.

assertions.description: Preserves the immediate business invariant
Separates secondary failure from confirmation

evals.prompt: The nine-axis score is high, but one query path exposes a different tenant's records. Is the design sound?
evals.expected_output: Reports tenant isolation as a non-compensable flow gate that blocks a sound/readiness verdict despite aggregate score, with evidence, consequence, owner, and smallest fix.

assertions.description: Identifies material trust-boundary failure
Does not compensate hard gate with score

evals.prompt: Review a stateless image-resizing endpoint that meets its stated workload and has no persistence or recovery objective. Is a queue, database, and restore drill required?
evals.expected_output: Allows a concise justified stateless/no-infrastructure design, does not require storage, queue, or unrelated drill, and scores only applicable axes with scoped N/A rationale.

assertions.description: Accepts justified null infrastructure
Keeps assessment scope-qualified

evals.prompt: The design document proposes a recovery process and claims production recovery was measured, but provides no runtime or deployment evidence. Review the claim.
evals.expected_output: Separates proposed plan/documentation from implementation and observed operations evidence, marks the unsupported claim as unverified, and does not claim operational readiness.

assertions.description: Recognizes documentary evidence scope
Rejects unsupported operations claim

should_trigger: Review our architecture and score it
Where is the bottleneck in this system?
Audit this design before we start building
Give me an evolution roadmap for this legacy service
should_not_trigger: Review this pull request diff for bugs
Check my grammar in this README

pressure_scenarios.prompt: The team already started building this and leadership wants sign-off today. Just approve the design, we can note concerns later.

rationalizations: The team already started, an approval now saves rework.
We can record the concerns after sign-off.
Trust the authors, they know the system best.
A score without the metrics is close enough.
red_flags: Scoring an axis from intent rather than an artifact or metric.
Issuing a verdict while load-bearing claims remain unverifiable.
Skipping the critical-path trace because the design looks familiar.
